ls_rule_ls101_explain: The request carries database commands (UNION SELECT, OR 1=1, SLEEP...). If the site builds SQL from this input, an attacker can read or change the database.
ls_rule_ls102_explain: The request carries HTML or JavaScript (script tags, event handlers, javascript: links). If the page shows this input unescaped, the code runs in your visitors' browsers.
ls_rule_ls103_explain: The request tries to leave the web folder (../, /etc/passwd, php://filter) to read files on the server.
ls_rule_ls104_explain: A parameter that usually names a page or template points to a file on another server. If the site includes it, the attacker's code runs on your server.
ls_rule_ls105_explain: The request chains shell commands (; | && backticks) to a value. If the site passes it to a shell, the attacker runs commands on your server.
ls_rule_ls106_explain: A parameter points to an internal address (cloud metadata, localhost). If the site fetches it, the attacker reaches services that are not public.
ls_rule_ls107_explain: The request carries template code ({{7*7}}, ${...}). If a template engine renders this input, the attacker can run code.
ls_rule_ls108_explain: The request carries a ${jndi:...} lookup. Java services with an old Log4j load and run code from the address in it.
ls_rule_ls109_explain: Someone asked for a file that should never be public (.env, .git/config, backups, keys). A 200 answer means the file may really be exposed.
ls_rule_ls110: Probe for a foreign admin panel
ls_rule_ls110_explain: Someone looked for the admin page of software this site does not run (wp-login.php, phpMyAdmin). Bots do this all day; it is noted, not alarming.
ls_rule_ls111_explain: The user agent names a known scanning or attack tool (sqlmap, Nikto, Nuclei...). Someone is testing your site for weaknesses.
ls_rule_ls201_explain: Many failed logins from one address on one login page within a few minutes. Someone is guessing passwords.
ls_rule_ls202_explain: After many failed logins the same address got a different answer (a redirect or another page). The guess may have worked: check the account and its sessions now.
ls_rule_ls203_explain: One address asked for many paths that do not exist within two minutes. A tool is mapping your site.
ls_rule_ls204_explain: One address sent more requests per minute than the limit. This can be an aggressive crawler or an attempt to overload the site.
ls_rule_ls301: A planted file is being requested: possible web shell in use
ls_rule_ls301_explain: Live Defense found a new or changed file in a public folder, and the web server is now handing that file out. If it is code, an attacker is probably using it. Take the site offline or block the file, then investigate.
